overview: After 1.Nc3 b5 Black offers the b-pawn, and 2.Nxb5 Bb7 then ...e6/...Nf6 gives Black a lead in development and pressure on e4/g2. White can keep the pawn but must return the knight to c3 and avoid ...Bxg2 tricks; compensation is limited.

white_ideas.idea: Take the pawn with Nxb5 and retreat Nc3
Play e4 and d4 for a big centre

black_ideas.idea: Use the b7 bishop on the long diagonal
Attack with ...Qb6 or ...a6 and open the b-file

typical_structures.structure: Open b-file for Black after the exchange
White has a healthy extra pawn and the centre

character.notes: A gambit with a quick bishop on b7 and open lines in exchange for a pawn.

gambit.notes: White can take on b5 and keep the pawn.

soundness.notes: Dubious for Black: the compensation is mostly a lead in development.

structure.notes: Mostly undecided centre; the b-file is open after the pawn is taken.

level.notes: A short line but a dubious one.

character.reason: Black gives a pawn for activity and the position can turn tactical quickly.

gambit.reason: Black offers the b-pawn and White can simply take it.

soundness.reason: Black has limited compensation for the pawn.

structure.reason: The b-file opens for Black while the centre is not yet fixed.

level.reason: It is dubious, so not Beginner, and relies on a few ideas.

plans.reason: The pawn is given for faster development and the b7 bishop.
